nodes.description: A patent document titled "Social medical network for diagnosis assistance" that describes a method and system for assisting medical diagnosis by exploiting similarity between new medical cases and existing cases and experts in a common embedding space.

nodes.entity_id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance
nodes.description: The title of patent US9589231B2, referring to a network-based approach for assisting diagnosis through similarity matching of medical cases and experts.
nodes.id: Social Medical Network For Diagnosis Assistance

nodes.description: A method that receives a query request including a new medical case, embeds the new case in an embedding space containing existing medical cases and experts, allows selection between query-for-cases and query-for-experts, and returns subsets based on computed similarity.

A multidimensional space in which new medical cases, existing medical cases, and experts are represented as multidimensional embeddings for similarity computation.<SEP>A common multidimensional space in which new medical cases, existing medical cases, and experts are embedded so that similarity between their representations can be computed.

A medical case submitted by a requester for which a diagnosis is sought, embedded in an embedding space for similarity comparison.<SEP>A medical case submitted by a requester in a query request, comprising a plurality of records relating to a specific patient, which is embedded in the embedding space for similarity comparison.

A set of prior medical cases embedded in the embedding space, used to identify similar cases for a new medical case.<SEP>A set of previously stored medical cases that are embedded in the embedding space and compared against a new medical case to return a similar subset.

A set of experts embedded in the embedding space who can be matched to a new medical case and attempt to provide a diagnosis.<SEP>A set of medical experts embedded in the embedding space based on information such as their profile, coded medical procedures performed, authored articles, and linked stored medical cases, who may be selected to formulate a diagnosis.

A user who submits a query request including a new medical case and selects from query types such as query-for-cases and query-for-experts.<SEP>A user who submits a query request including a new medical case and selects from available query types.

A query type that returns a subset of existing medical cases based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.<SEP>A query type that, when selected, returns a subset of existing medical cases based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded existing cases.

A query type that returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.<SEP>A query type that, when selected, returns a subset of experts based on computed similarity between the embedded new case and the embedded experts.

A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts differs from the cost for a query-for-cases.<SEP>A computed cost for a query, where the cost for a query-for-experts differs from and is higher than the cost for a query-for-cases, encouraging requesters to try query-by-cases first.

A structure comprising a set of medical concepts joined by links, each concept corresponding to a dimension in the multidimensional representation, used as the basis for embedding medical cases and experts.

A representation of medical cases and experts generated in the embedding space, used to compute similarities.<SEP>A computed representation of a medical case based on a medical ontology, used to embed the case in the embedding space.
A matrix applied to the multidimensional representation of a new case that accounts for relationships between concepts in the ontology when computing similarity measures.
A system on which the medical ontology may be based.
One of the categories of concepts that the ontology may include.

Information about an expert used as a basis for embedding the expert in the embedding space.

Articles authored by an expert, used as a basis for embedding the expert.
